shouldFix.class: heading records an operative limb the entry's own body denies, with no disclaimer
shouldFix.defect: The recorded heading is 'D-360 - Record platform-tcb-contract.v47 as DR-126 C4-c application-grade TCB successor', and the Decision repeats it verbatim: 'Record platform-tcb-contract.v47 as DR-126 C4-c application-grade TCB successor after D-359.' Inside COORD, C4-c already has one adopted gloss. Adopted D-341 (COORD lines 20738-20739) reads: 'C4-c (application-grade TCB successor making the grammar governing) and C4-d (complete profile population) are not this act.' D-293 item 6 (COORD lines 16245-16248) is the source: 'owner assignment, then an application-grade TCB successor that makes the grammar governing, then complete profile population.' So within COORD the phrase 'C4-c application-grade TCB successor' denotes the successor that makes the grammar governing. The subject's own body denies every operative element of that: 'The candidate binds NOTHING. DR-126 stays OPEN. G22 stays not QUALIFIED. Selector values and per-OS profiles stay RESERVED.' (line 83), 'Condition-4 effect is zero.' (line 83), and 'Does not choose a binds value reviewers have not granted.' (line 35). The measured subject of the recording matches the denial, not the heading: platform-tcb-contract.v47.json carries status CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, binds NOTHING, sealRecommendation DO-NOT-SEAL. The recorded C4 plan states the same test - DECISION-PACKETS/C-plan/C4-dr126-tcb-owner-grammar-profiles.md section 1, limb (c) row, asks 'Does an artifact carry a token that must change?' and answers 'Yes - $.status/$.binds and every RESERVED selector standing'. v47 changes none of the three. The entry carries a 34-item disclaimer list that reaches 'Does not invent Rosetta' and 'Does not invent Windows', but carries neither 'Does not make the TCB selector grammar governing' nor 'Does not complete C4-c', and does not qualify the heading noun with 'candidate'.
shouldFix.precedent: D-341, the immediately preceding C4 act on this lineage, carries the disclaimer explicitly: 'Does not make the TCB selector grammar governing.' The frozen Stage A record draws the same line and puts the completing act exactly here: platform-tcb-contract.v46.review-independent.claude2.json c4StageAudit rules the C4-c framing 'honest for a CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED' only because "authorityClaim's verb is PROPOSES", and its whatThisVerdictDoesNotDo[13] reads 'Does not complete C4-c or C4-d; recording this subject is a later coordinator act.' D-360 is that later coordinator act, and it drops the verb the Stage A ruling relied on. The subject artifact keeps it: platform-tcb-contract.v47.json authorityClaim opens 'platform-tcb-contract.v47 PROPOSES the C4-c application-grade successor'. The lineage's own recording headings qualify the noun where the artifact binds nothing: D-125 'Record platform-tcb-contract.v45 as DR-126 leftover T2-02 candidate', D-126 / D-128 / D-129 / D-130 / D-131 'as ... successor candidate', D-137 'as DR-117's preview-scoped successor candidate'.
shouldFix.whyItMatters: An adopted COORD heading is the permanent citation. A later reader who resolves 'C4-c' against COORD's only gloss of it - D-341's - reads this heading as recording that the application-grade TCB successor making the grammar governing has been recorded, and therefore that C4-c is discharged and C4 has advanced to C4-d. D-293 item 6 sequences G22's reservation on exactly that ordering. The entry's body says the opposite in its first four sentences, so the record would carry a heading and a body that answer the same question differently.
shouldFix.loadBearing: No. The Decision fixes binds NOTHING, DR-126 OPEN, G22 not QUALIFIED, selectors RESERVED and Condition-4 effect zero in its first sentences, so a reader of the whole entry is not misled about the live state; no status token, count, owner cell, digest or obligation is misstated. Only the heading, read alone or grepped, carries the overclaim. That is why this is SHOULD-FIX and not MUST-FIX.
shouldFix.repair: Either qualify the noun in the heading and in the first Decision sentence - 'as DR-126 C4-c application-grade TCB successor candidate' - or keep the heading and add the D-341-form disclaimer to the list, 'Does not make the TCB selector grammar governing. Does not complete C4-c.' Change nothing else: not the digests, the Stage A recitals, the advisory handling, the readiness numbers, or the Reversibility limb.

shouldFix.class: Reversibility limb cites the wrong occupancy recording; the heading the entry expressly preserves is absent and an unrelated one is present
shouldFix.defect: Line 41 preserves an artifact by name: 'Does not remasure occupancy v2.' It sits inside an unbroken run of DR-126 / G22 clauses (lines 38-43: platform-tcb leftover-join.v9, platform-tcb leftover-join.v10, leftover-join.v5 of G22, occupancy v2, platform-tcb-contract.v45, platform-tcb-contract.v46), so 'occupancy v2' is the G22 occupancy, harness.DR-G22.platform-abi-loader.v2.json, whose recording heading is 'D-219 - Record harness.DR-G22.platform-abi-loader.v2 as G22 occupancy remasurement' (C4 plan section 2.4 pins the same identification). Line 91 does not name D-219. It names D-218 instead: 'Does not unwrite D-086, D-125, D-218, D-268, D-271, D-293, D-314, D-315, D-316, D-341, D-347, D-356, D-357, D-358, or D-359.' D-218 is 'Record harness.DR-G21.component-failure-containment.v4 as G21 occupancy remasurement' - a G21 occupancy the entry never mentions at any of its 91 lines. Every other member of that list is the recording heading of something the entry expressly preserves: D-086 (required-now naming), D-125 (platform-tcb-contract.v45, line 42), D-268 (platform-tcb leftover-join.v9, line 38), D-271 (leftover-join.v5 of G22, line 40), D-293 / D-314 / D-315 (user decisions), D-316 (cited in the Decision), D-341 (the prior C4 act), D-347 (leftover-join.v14 of sarif, line 45), D-356-D-359 (the G21 chain and leftover-join.v45 of G21, lines 44, 48-49). D-218 is the single member with no such clause, and D-219 is the single preservation clause with no such member.
shouldFix.precedent: D-341, the prior act on this same lineage, gets it right: 'Does not unwrite D-125, D-219, D-268, D-271, D-293, D-294, D-314, or D-340.' D-219 is in that list, D-218 is not. D-218 is in the Reversibility list of the immediately preceding draft, coordinator-decisions.D-359.draft.md line 135, which is a G21 act whose subject chain runs through G21 occupancy v4 - but D-360 carries none of the rest of that G21 list (D-241, D-243, D-245, D-247, D-285, D-292, D-301, D-302, D-324, D-335-D-338, D-348-D-355), so D-218 arrives alone from the predecessor rather than from this entry's own subject matter.
shouldFix.whyItMatters: The Reversibility limb is where the entry states which recorded headings its overturn does not disturb, and this entry's readers will use it to see which recordings the C4-c step sits on top of. As written it protects a G21 occupancy this decision never touches while leaving unnamed the G22 occupancy remasurement whose standing the entry expressly relies on one line above the DR-126 contract clauses. On a DR-126 / G22 entry that is a one-digit substitution away from the lineage-correct list D-341 already recorded.
shouldFix.loadBearing: No. 'Does not unwrite D-218' is a true sentence, and omitting D-219 states nothing false; the overturn scope is C-D360 either way, and no digest, count, status token or owner cell depends on the list. The defect is that the recorded citation points at the wrong lineage. That is why this is SHOULD-FIX and not MUST-FIX.
shouldFix.repair: Name D-219 in the Reversibility list in place of D-218, matching D-341's list for this lineage; or, if the G21 chain reference is intended, keep D-219 and add D-218 with the rest of the G21 chain rather than alone. Change nothing else in the limb - not C-D360, not the other fourteen headings.
